name: Bear crawl
summary: On hands and feet with the knees hovering, crawl forward moving opposite hand and foot together.
setup: Hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips and lifted a few centimetres. Move the right hand and left foot forward together, then the other pair, keeping the back flat and the hips low.
why: Crawling takes you out of frame. Logged by hand.

faults.label: Hips rising
faults.tip: Imagine a plate balanced on the lower back.

faults.label: Hips too high
faults.tip: The knees stay a few centimetres off the floor; high hips make it a walk.

faults.label: Hips swaying
faults.cue: Move the hips as little as possible
faults.tip: Shorter steps keep the hips still.

faults.label: Same-side hand and foot
faults.tip: Opposite limbs move together; same-side crawling loses the anti-rotation work.

guide.cannotSee: You — the exercise crawls out of frame.
